English: Camel Tether Post
A simple arrangement of posts and ropes for securing caravans' camels on the open steppe, allowing for basic rest and organization.
Desert Tent
A large, weather-resistant tent woven from camel hair, offering shade and shelter to travelers and merchants passing through the harsh desert.
Pack Animal Shelter
A rudimentary lean-to of palm fronds and timber, protecting horses, donkeys, and camels from the desert sun and sandstorms.
Traders’ Pavilion
A spacious, multi-sectioned tent for itinerant traders to display wares, exchange news, and strike deals under the protection of the caravanserai.
Walled Camp
A fortified enclosure of mudbrick and timber, providing protection for travelers, animals, and merchants against raiders and sandstorms.
Merchants Hall
A permanent wooden hall, serving as headquarters for influential traders and a meeting site for merchant councils to negotiate trade and security.
Camel Stable
A purpose-built adobe structure for housing camels, with watering troughs and feed bins, ensuring the health and readiness of caravan beasts.
Market Pavilion
A covered market of wooden stalls and stone columns, attracting distant caravans and local traders to exchange rare goods and luxuries.
Trade Storage Room
A secure stone chamber for safeguarding coin, rare wares, and merchant ledgers, reducing losses to theft and weather.
Arabic Grand Caravanserai
A monumental, fortified caravanserai of stone and tile, with a vast inner courtyard, public baths, stables, and merchant lodgings—a vital hub for transcontinental trade and clan unity.
